title: EMINOV v. "THE FORMER YUGOSLAV REPUBLIC OF MACEDONIA"
summary: In the case of Eminov v. "the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia," the applicant, Mr. Eminov, identified as a member of the Roma community, brought a complaint against the Macedonian state. The case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma individuals in seeking justice for alleged violations of their fundamental rights, a context where Roma and Travellers have historically faced barriers to effective remedies. Mr. Eminov’s application concerned serious allegations, including potential violations of Article 2 (right to life) and Article 13 (right to an effective remedy) of the European Convention on Human Rights, though the specific facts of the incident were not detailed in the Court’s final decision. During the proceedings, the Government offered a friendly settlement, agreeing to pay Mr. Eminov 9,000 euros in compensation for non-pecuniary damage, with clear terms for payment and interest in case of delay. The European Court of Human Rights accepted this settlement, finding it consistent with respect for human rights, and struck the case out of its list under Article 39. This outcome is significant as it demonstrates the potential for friendly settlements to provide redress for Roma applicants, reflecting ongoing efforts to address historical injustices and improve access to justice for Roma and Traveller communities in Europe.
